quick.topic: Test data at the front door
quick.summary: Catch bad data before it flows downstream and breaks your reports.
quick.takeaway: Test data right when it lands. Do not wait for things to break.

parts.title: Test data at the front door

beats.line: We spent hours fixing a report. Someone loaded future dates. How did that happen?

board.text: Test data at the front door

beats.line: You let the dirt into the house before checking if it was clean.
We ran tests after the report broke.
Exactly. You need a filter at the main valve. Like in a house.
Test the data early. Stop it if it looks wrong.
Engineers call this data quality assertions.
Can I just say front door checks?
So I check if dates are real right at the source. Otherwise, halt.

quiz.question: When is the best time to run a check on incoming data?
options: Right after it enters the system.
Once a week on the weekend.
quiz.explanation: Checking data at the source prevents bad information from traveling downstream and ruining other processes.

quiz.question: Data checks are only useful for finding out why a report already failed.
quiz.explanation: Data checks should act as a front door filter, stopping bad data before it causes failures.
